explanation: Asia covers about 44.5 million km² — roughly a third of the world's land area, and more than four times the size of Europe.
Asia is home to roughly 60% of the world's population — China and India alone account for close to a third of everyone alive.
Oceania — Australia plus the Pacific islands — covers roughly 8.5 million km², smaller than every other continent, including Europe.
James Naismith invented basketball in 1891 in Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.
Moscow sits in European Russia, west of the Ural Mountains that mark the conventional border with Asia.
Europe's median age is around 42–43 — the oldest of any continent, ahead of North America.
Africa's median age is around 19–20, by far the youngest of any continent.
Australia alone has roughly 70 million sheep against about 26 million people — more than two sheep per person.
Australia has well over 200 marsupial species — kangaroos, koalas and wombats among them — far more than the opossums of the Americas.
The United States alone records more tornadoes than any other country, concentrated in the central "Tornado Alley" region.
Potatoes were first domesticated in the Andes, in what is now Peru and Bolivia, thousands of years ago.
Antarctica's interior receives less than 50mm of precipitation a year, making it the driest continent on Earth despite all its ice.
Antarctica's katabatic winds, which pour downhill off the ice sheet, make it the windiest continent on average.
Bolivia and Paraguay are South America's only landlocked countries — every other continent with landlocked countries has more than two.

clue: Has the most area covered by lakes
explanation: Canada alone holds roughly 60% of the world's lakes, and together with the Great Lakes it gives North America more lake area than any other continent.
Asia's combined GDP — led by China, Japan and India — is now the largest of any continent, especially by purchasing power.
South America has around 3,500 recorded bird species — more than any other continent — with Colombia, Peru and Brazil leading the count.
European nations have won well over half of all Summer Olympic gold medals in history, far ahead of any other continent.

clue: Birthplace of most of the world's top 100 marathoners
explanation: East African countries — above all Kenya and Ethiopia — produce the overwhelming majority of the world's fastest marathon runners.
